intro.text: Review window: 2026-07-22 through 2026-07-28. The review covered the focused image/video discovery feeds and direct checks of official image generation, video generation/editing, digital-human, dubbing/localization, virtual try-on, audio/video, 3D, unified-generation, and Physical-AI sources.

items: **Artificial Analysis image-to-video ranking:** Dreamina Seedance 2.0 720p moved from rank 2 to rank 1, while Gemini Omni Flash moved from rank 1 to rank 2. All current Top-15 entries still resolve to verified model cards; the provider snapshot is used only as evidence for this observed ranking. [Official leaderboard](https://artificialanalysis.ai/video/leaderboard/image-to-video)

**Dailymotion source platform:** the official developer portal now identifies API v2 as the current recommended interface and documents authenticated upload and content management, delivery, players, advertising, analytics, and reporting. The platform profile now names API v2 and retains the existing boundary that API access does not grant model-training rights. [Official API v2 documentation](https://developers.dailymotion.com/docs/welcome)

**Monitor reliability:** the GPT Image 2 probe now follows OpenAI's stable first-party system-card PDF after the API model page returned an empty normalized body and the release page rejected the scanner. UniSync, iTryOn, and HoliDubber now use their official arXiv paper or abstract pages instead of rate-limited export API queries. These changes improve revision monitoring without changing any model or dataset fact. [GPT Image 2 system card](https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/chatgpt-images-2-0/chatgpt-images-2-0.pdf) · [UniSync](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.03882) · [iTryOn](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21431) · [HoliDubber](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09098)

blocks.text: All nine machine candidates were opened at their primary source. None supports a new catalog card or model–dataset relationship in this review.

items: Excluded as medical generation survey/evaluation rather than maintained generative-media training data: [medical inpainting survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21904) and [Medical-Checklist](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21998).

Excluded as multimodal understanding, fake-image detection, visual relocalization, or watermarking rather than media-generation data strategy: [small-VLM confidence under degradation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22034), [FAIR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22087), [sparse-view relocalization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22147), and [latent angular watermarking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22386).

Not promoted because the work is an inference-time guidance method or an interactive art tool and does not release a new training corpus: [Spectral Alignment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22091) and [interactive model bending](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22428).

Excluded because the Hugging Face entry is an unofficial third-party modified FLUX text encoder, not an organization release or first-party data disclosure: [ponpoke/flux2-klein-4b-uncensored-text-encoder](https://huggingface.co/ponpoke/flux2-klein-4b-uncensored-text-encoder).

blocks.text: The PosterCraft organization still exposes the same two public repositories, Text-Render-2M and Poster100K, with the same approximate row counts and no new component license or access conclusion. Google model pages for Gemini 3 Pro Image, Gemini 3.1 Flash Image, and Veo 3.1 Lite changed content hashes but did not add training-corpus or model-specific data-pipeline disclosures. Meta's blog change was caused by newer perception/robotics posts and did not change Muse Video access or training information.

The current OpenAI, Alibaba Cloud, and PixVerse pages likewise add no named training datasets, mixture sizes, provenance, license inventory, filtering, deduplication, relabeling, synthetic-data, or preference-optimization facts for GPT Image 1.5/2, HappyHorse 1.0/1.1, Wan 2.6/2.7, Qwen-Image 2.0, or PixVerse V6. Pexels continues to require explicit permission for API-backed dataset construction or ML/AI use, so its existing rights-review boundary is unchanged.

Physical-AI checks found two new Meta deployment stories about SAM/DINO use in scientific imaging and assistive robotics. They describe perception-model deployment and downstream auto-labeling/fine-tuning, not a newly released action model, generative world model, simulation corpus, or downloadable robot dataset, so they remain outside the catalog's generative/action-data boundary: [Genesis Mission](https://ai.meta.com/blog/genesis-mission-lawrence-berkeley-national-laboratory-segment-anything-dino/) · [assistive robotics](https://ai.meta.com/blog/assistive-robotics-university-of-pittsburgh-sam-dino/).

No reviewed revision supplies a new model-development dataset name, download, weight release, technical report, mixture ratio, rights composition, scale, cleaning or deduplication recipe, relabeling process, synthetic-data recipe, or preference-training corpus. Existing unknowns therefore remain explicit on the affected model cards, and no `last_verified` field is advanced solely because a page hash changed.

The final live review pass checked all 298 watched first-party sources with zero source failures, zero recoveries, and zero ranked-model coverage gaps. It retained the nine reviewed candidates and one image-to-video ranking change until the reviewed discovery baseline was accepted.

sections.title: Dataset-detail repair and same-day model/data intake

blocks.text: The OpenVE-Edit screenshot reported in review came from the retired preview deployment: its footer knew that two catalog relations existed, but that older JavaScript bundle did not render the relation rows. The maintained GitHub Pages build now shows **OpenVE-3M** and **OpenVE-Bench** by name, with separate “view data card” and direct Hugging Face access actions. A durable `#strategy-datasets-openve-edit` hash restores the correct strategy view; each dataset also has its own `#dataset-*` deep link. The old `aigc-datahub-index.zuotongbin.chatgpt.site` address remains outside the GitHub deployment pipeline and should not be used for verification.
This review also resolves five more model references that previously appeared only as prose:

items: **SANA-Video 2.0** now links to an unavailable progressive-training card and an unavailable preference-pair card. The first records the paper's approximately 30M pretraining, 10M continual-training, and 10K SFT clip stages without incorrectly summing potentially overlapping pools. The second records Gemini-ranked generated comparisons while leaving the undisclosed pair count unknown.

**Mage-Flow** is corrected from “announced” to an MIT open-weight family after Microsoft released code and six generation/editing checkpoints. Its 1.3B curated image-text corpus, 45M retained editing triples, and approximately 50K generation/editing RL prompts now have separate cards. All three remain unavailable as data even though the model artifacts are public.

blocks.text: The live discovery pass then found eleven new arXiv candidates and one ranking change. Eight candidates were excluded as medical understanding, fake-image detection, watermarking, view localization, surveys, or interactive art tools outside the core generation-data scope. Three were promoted from primary papers:

items: **InnoText ↔ InnoText-30K:** a paper-only unified visual-text generation and editing model plus its unreleased 20K-Chinese / 10K-English corpus, assembled from Lex-10K, a Seedream-generated Chinese counterpart, and an AnyWord-3M subset.

**AgentHOI ↔ AgentHOI Mixed-Source Training Corpus:** public checkpoints and code with no declared repository license, linked to an unreleased 108K-clip corpus containing 71K real clips mined from 10M online videos and 37K synthetic clips.

**fMRI2Face ↔ fMRI-Face:** a paper-only neural video decoder linked to 62,856 fMRI–digital-human video pairs from three consenting subjects. The card explicitly treats brain signals as sensitive personal data and does not imply access from publication alone.

blocks.text: The monitor also captured Recraft V4.1 Utility moving from rank 13 to 12 and Grok Imagine Image Quality moving from 12 to 13 on the watched text-to-image board. The catalog now contains 113 datasets, 91 models, 129 explicit model-to-dataset role relations, 27 dataset-lineage relations, and 298 watched first-party sources.

sections.title: WorldWeaver and Solaris multi-agent world-model lineage

blocks.text: The catalog now follows a complete public-to-unreleased data chain instead of recording WorldWeaver as an isolated new paper:

items: **WorldWeaver** is linked to a dedicated card for its approximately 126-hour synchronized two-agent Minecraft corpus. The paper documents 832x480 video at 20 FPS, per-agent state and controller logs, a shared overhead camera, and Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct scene text for every four-frame chunk. The card is deliberately marked unavailable because no files, download path, dataset license, code, or checkpoints have been published.

**Solaris** is added as the open-weight upstream multiplayer world model. Its runnable four-stage pipeline links the public VPT contractor demonstrations, the public 12.64M-frame / 9,240-episode Solaris Training Dataset, and the public 1,280-row Solaris Eval Datasets. The inherited Matrix Game 2.0 corpus remains an unresolved reference rather than being guessed from the base checkpoint name.

**Solaris Training Dataset** and **Solaris Eval Datasets** have direct Hugging Face download actions. Their official Apache-2.0 declarations are recorded, while Minecraft/Mojang media-rights review remains separate from repository licensing. **VPT Contractor Demonstrations** points to OpenAI's official MP4 and JSONL indices and explicitly distinguishes that public release from the 70,000-hour online-video corpus in the original VPT pipeline.

WorldWeaver's evaluation edge resolves to the Solaris test release used by the paper, while its inherited single-player video prior remains unknown. Thus the detail view shows both navigable cards and unresolved evidence boundaries instead of turning every named input into a fake download.

blocks.text: Six new critical probes watch both model repositories and all four dataset surfaces. The monitor now parses arXiv Atom feeds from stable entry version and entry-update fields rather than hashing the dynamic query timestamp, eliminating false paper-revision alerts. Default scan concurrency is reduced to improve Hugging Face reliability; baseline acceptance still fails closed on any source failure.

The catalog now contains 105 datasets, 88 models, 121 explicit model-to-dataset role relations, 27 dataset-lineage relations, and 287 watched first-party sources. The accepted 287-source live scan completed with zero new candidates, important revisions, source failures, recoveries, ranking changes, or ranking coverage gaps.

blocks.text: ElasticTTT is now represented as three separate evidence layers so the strategy view no longer makes a per-run input look like a missing downloadable corpus:

items: **Inherited pretraining data:** the method reuses a Wan video diffusion backbone, but the ElasticTTT paper does not enumerate that base model's full source corpus or mixture. This remains an unresolved pretraining reference.

sections.title: Cinematic dubbing and production lip-sync lineage

blocks.text: Three recent systems now expose their data strategy as navigable model ↔ dataset relations instead of leaving dataset names inside paper prose:

items: **DiFlowDubber** pretrains a zero-shot TTS prior on a disclosed 470-hour LibriTTS subset, then adapts separate models on Chem and GRID. LibriTTS and GRID have official download surfaces; Chem does not. The official repository remains a paper/project shell and still marks implementation and checkpoints as coming soon.

**FunCineForge** trains its main 0.5B cinematic-dubbing system on CineDub-CN, a 7.2 TB internal corpus distilled from more than 6,000 raw Chinese television hours into 1,559,172 samples and more than 4,700 effective speech hours. The code and bilingual checkpoint are public, but the full corpus is not. The separately released CineDub-Example repository is gated, non-commercial, and contains roughly 52.93 GB of Chinese and English examples; it is not presented as the complete training set. A controlled comparison links the model to V2C-Animation, Chem, and GRID for both training and evaluation roles.

**UniSync** fine-tunes an undisclosed audio-image-to-video base model on a named but unreleased 5,000-video high-resolution corpus. It evaluates on HDTF and the new 495-video RealWorld-LipSync benchmark. The paper promises the new benchmark for future public release, but no files, repository, weights, or license are currently available.

blocks.text: The acquisition layer keeps four states separate: direct official downloads (LibriTTS and GRID), reconstruction metadata without redistributable media (V2C-Animation), gated examples (CineDub-Example), project/metadata-only corpora (Chem and CineDub-CN), and paper-only unavailable corpora (UniSync 5K and RealWorld-LipSync). Eleven new critical probes watch every added model and dataset surface for repository, checkpoint, file, access, or license changes.

sections.title: Important model and dataset revision monitoring

blocks.text: The weekly scanner now watches 97 official sources. Twenty-nine are first-party dataset revision endpoints for high-value image-text, video, dubbing, Try-On, audio, 3D, and evaluation corpora, and thirteen track stable revisions of cataloged open or research models. Hugging Face probes use the pair of `lastModified` and repository commit SHA; official GitHub probes use commit date and SHA. After the first reviewed baseline, any change opens the same triage Issue as a new model candidate.

Pick-a-Pic v2 remains a catalog card, but its gated API returned HTTP 401 in an unauthenticated GitHub Actions context, so it is not used as a revision probe. DataComp-1B replaces it in this automated set with a publicly readable official dataset API. Access and license review for Pick-a-Pic v2 still follows the 90-day freshness policy.

Two maintainer-provided internal inventories were used as discovery leads, not as public evidence. Internal storage paths, download status, private corpora, and unverified scale estimates were intentionally excluded. Every accepted card below was rebuilt from a public paper, project page, repository, or official Hugging Face release.

sections.title: Industry ranking and new-dataset release monitoring

blocks.text: This iteration adds a second discovery channel for head-model coverage. Five Artificial Analysis leaderboards are snapshotted weekly: text-to-image, image editing, text-to-video, image-to-video, and video editing. The scanner keeps up to fifteen positions per board, including both open-weight and closed/API models, and alerts only on membership or ordering changes rather than ordinary Elo movement. The reviewed baseline currently contains 66 ranking positions; every current Top 5 entry maps to a canonical model card.

Twelve model versions were added from first-party release, API, or investor sources: GPT Image 2, GPT Image 1.5, Reve 2.1, MAI-Image-2.5, Gemini 3.1 Flash Image, Gemini 3 Pro Image, Wan 2.7, HappyHorse 1.0, HappyHorse 1.1, Grok Imagine Video 1.5, Runway Aleph 2.0, and Kling AI 3.0. Their release dates are recorded at the exact version level and the generated model index is explicitly sorted newest-first. None of these sources publishes identifiable training-dataset names, so their cards retain an `undisclosed` corpus instead of inventing lineage.

Eight Hugging Face dataset API feeds sorted by creation time now cover text-to-image, image generation, text-to-video, video generation, image-to-video, talking heads, video dubbing, and virtual try-on. The first reviewed snapshot contains 142 release candidates. Together with arXiv recent feeds and vendor/research sources, the full scanner now watches 116 sources with zero baseline failures.

`MODEL_DATASET_INDEX.md` is now generated and checked in CI. It lists all 41 models and every data reference: 26 resolve to catalog cards, while 51 rows explain that the source is unreleased or undisclosed. Validation rejects any future `public` or `gated` named reference without a canonical catalog card. The site adds a ranking view, ranking badges on mapped model cards, visible resolution reasons on unlinked data references, and an explicit “release date: new to old” ordering label.

The link audit also replaced two stale 404 release-date declarations for HDTF and CelebV-HQ with live first-party evidence. Confirmed 404/410 responses remain hard failures; rate limits, anti-bot responses, and transient connection errors are reported separately as warnings.
